Text.Text: The Reaver chief is dead, his dig is lost, and his buyers will wait for a shipment that never comes. You controlled the fight instead of feeding it. That is the beginning of Hunger of the Dark. Sit. The rest of the lesson is mine to give.

You want to be fed before you can hold the spoon. Your command of the Force is not ready for what waits on Korriban. Go and sharpen it. When the Force comes to you without begging, find me at this table again.

The Vitae Reavers have found a buyer for relics they barely understand. To fuel their dig in the Korriban Sith Crypt Depths, they drain the survey crews they caught down there, life and all. Crude. Wasteful. That makes them my business, and perhaps yours. Put down six Vitae Reaver Initiates and bring me the Hunger of the Dark Crypt Trial Tablet they took from the tombs.
Take this key. It opens the sealed passage at the north end of the Sith Crypt on Korriban, the way into the Depths. Six initiates, and the tablet. Take only what you need from them.

Hunger of the Dark is the discipline of taking strength from a fight and spending only what the moment demands. The Reavers drain everything in reach and choke on it. Watch them, learn what not to do, and never mistake their excess for mastery.

Korriban. From the starport, go east into the Wastelands North and cross to the elevator on the north-east side of the wastes. It takes you down into the Sith Crypt; the sealed passage at the crypt's north end opens into the Depths. I stay because their buyers drink here in Anchorhead. While you cut the supply, I will starve the market.

An independent band of Force-trained relic thieves, with no academy commission and no master worth the name. Their initiates use stolen draining techniques on anyone who comes close. Their enforcer and their chief are Cathar, and they have bought Wookiee muscle to hold the deeper vaults.
Six Vitae Reaver Initiates and the tablet. The passage is at the north end of the Sith Crypt on Korriban. They will not starve themselves.
You have the Hunger of the Dark Crypt Trial Tablet. Set it on the table.
Etched with the tombs they have emptied, and the ones they mean to empty next. Their adepts have moved deeper with the relics. Eat. Rest. You will need both.

The initiates were the first course. Their adepts carry the Hunger of the Dark Ritual Focus Shard, a relic that lets them draw more than their bodies can hold. Put down five Vitae Reaver Adepts and bring the shard to me before one of them learns to use it properly.
Five Vitae Reaver Adepts and the focus shard. They hunt the Depths in small packs. Let them come to you.

The shard sharpens a hunger into a blade. In a disciplined hand it is a tool. In theirs it is a crutch, and it is how they drain the crews so quickly. Take it, and they go back to being greedy amateurs.
Nowhere fixed. The adepts range through the Depths in small packs, and one of them always carries the shard. Thin the packs and it will come to you.
They drain together, feeding one another. Break the chain. Finish the one who is drawing first, and do not let them feed on you while you are wounded.
Five Vitae Reaver Adepts and the shard, somewhere in the Korriban Sith Crypt Depths. They are still feeding.
You brought the Hunger of the Dark Ritual Focus Shard. Give it here. Slowly.
It still hums with what they took. I will see it emptied properly. Their enforcer is next, and he will not be a light meal.

Their enforcer, a Cathar who goes by Vitae Reaver Enforcer, guards the trial altar on the east side of the Depths. He broke the Hunger of the Dark Splintered Tomb Sigil off a sealed tomb, and he keeps it on him. Go to that altar and he will come to meet you. Bring at least two allies. Bring me the sigil.
Good. The altar is on the east side of the Korriban Sith Crypt Depths. Make him come to you, let your allies wear him down, and take the sigil when he falls.
A Cathar, the best they have. He has drained enough of the crews to stand through wounds that would drop most fighters. They placed him at the altar to keep anyone from following the dig.
It was broken off a sealed tomb entrance. The markings will tell me which tomb they forced and what they carried out of it. Their buyers would like to know that too. They will not get the chance.
Because a lone fighter is exactly what the enforcer feeds on. Three of you can split his attention and keep one another standing. Hunger without discipline dies alone. You will not.
The enforcer still holds the altar on the east side of the Depths. Two allies at your side, then the sigil.
You brought the Hunger of the Dark Splintered Tomb Sigil. Show me.
There. The tomb they forced, and the ones they have not reached. With the enforcer gone, only their binders stand between us and their chief.

Four Wookiees, the ones they call Vitae Reaver Binders, now hold the way to the deep vaults. They carry the Hunger of the Dark Keeper's Rite Token, an old keeper's mark that opens the last sealed chambers. Put down four Vitae Reaver Binders and bring me the token.
Four Vitae Reaver Binders and the token. They range through the Depths. Take them one at a time.
Wookiees, bound to the Reavers by debt and kept loyal with stolen strength. They do the heavy work of the dig and the heavy work of killing. Do not pity them.
The tomb keepers carried it once. It opens the deepest vaults. As long as the Reavers hold it, nothing below is closed to them.
Never let all four reach you together. Choose your ground, keep your allies close, and watch the passage behind you. A Wookiee who has fed on the Force does not tire easily.
Four Vitae Reaver Binders and the token, somewhere in the Korriban Sith Crypt Depths.
You brought the Hunger of the Dark Keeper's Rite Token. Set it down.
Good. The vaults stay shut. Only their chief remains, and he has nowhere left to run.

Their chief, a Cathar they call the Vitae Reaver Chief, has taken the last relics into the Final Ritual Chamber, through the door at the north end of the Depths. He has been drinking from the crews for weeks, and he will be strong. Bring at least two allies and end him before he moves the shipment.
Go together. The Final Ritual Chamber is through the north door of the Korriban Sith Crypt Depths. Take what you need from the fight, and nothing more.
The chief himself, gorged on what he drained from the crews and on the relics around him. Break him there, and the surviving crews can walk out.
He draws on the stolen relics and on everyone near him. He will try to wear you down and feed on whoever falters. Stay close, keep each other standing, and give him no moment's rest.
I finish with their buyers here in Anchorhead. Once the chief is gone, there is no shipment left to buy. When you return, the records you recovered will tell us what they stole, and who wanted it.
The Vitae Reaver Chief waits in the Final Ritual Chamber, at the north end of the Depths. Take your allies.
The Vitae Reaver Chief is down. Tell me how it went.

The Reaver chief is dead, his dig is lost, and his buyers will wait for a shipment that never comes. You controlled the fight instead of feeding it. That is the beginning of Hunger of the Dark. Sit. The rest of the lesson is mine to give.

Junix's Joint in Anchorhead has customers who know better than to ask who taught a stranger. My lessons are no academy commission, and I don't care whose banner you carry. I care whether you can control what you take. The Vitae Reavers are in the Korriban Sith Crypt Depths on Korriban. Bring their records back to this table on Tatooine.
Go over the first assignment.
I'll go down and bring back the tablet.
What does this discipline teach?
Where do I go, and why are you staying here?
Who or what will I be fighting?
I need to prepare first.
Here is the recovered tablet.
Go over the next objective.
I will recover the focus shard.
Why does the shard matter?
Where do they keep it?
How do they fight?
I need more time.
Here is the focus shard.
Go over the enforcer again.
I'll bring two allies and take the sigil.
Who is the enforcer?
Why recover the broken sigil?
Why bring a group?
I will gather my companions first.
The enforcer is dead. Here is the sigil.
Go over the four Binders again.
I'll deal with the four Binders.
Who are these Binders?
What does the token do?
How should we approach them?
I need to rest first.
Here is the recovered token.
Go over the final objective.
We will go in together.
What is waiting in the last chamber?
What makes the leader dangerous?
What happens after this?
My companions need to prepare.
The final target is down. We made it out.
Why are we meeting here, and where is the trial?
Back to the assignment.
